name: Trailing Nasturtium
variety: Trailing garden-nasturtium horticultural type; no named cultivar specified
summary: A trailing type of garden nasturtium, botanically distinct from bush nasturtium (Tropaeolum minus). University of Wisconsin Extension documents its cascading use, edible leaves and flowers, and seed propagation; no specific cultivar is represented.

identity.short: Trailing garden type of Tropaeolum majus
identity.guidance: Kew accepts Tropaeolum majus. Wisconsin Extension distinguishes trailing T. majus from bush T. minus. This identity represents the trailing horticultural type, not a cultivar or every product sold as nasturtium.

cultivation.short: Full sun supports flowering; partial shade can reduce bloom
cultivation.guidance: Wisconsin Extension recommends well-drained soil and full sun, noting plants grow in partial shade but flower less well. Trailing types suit hanging baskets, window boxes, or a wall edge; the article says they do not climb well on their own. This is garden/container guidance, not evidence of hydroponic suitability.

growth.guidance: The extension source describes trailing forms and cautions that so-called climbing nasturtiums lack tendrils and do not climb well without help. Trim only when the plant is crowding nearby plants; no fixed pruning schedule is claimed.

harvest.short: Young leaves and flowers are edible
harvest.guidance: Wisconsin Extension describes leaves and flowers as edible, with a peppery flavor; young leaves are preferred because older leaves can be bitter. This is culinary-use information, not a medicinal claim.

problems.guidance: Wisconsin Extension identifies aphids, imported cabbageworm caterpillars, and leafminers among observed pests; it notes leafminer trails usually do not damage the plant. Inspect first and avoid treating cosmetic trails as severe injury.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: Garden/container guidance does not establish long-term hydroponic production.

evidence.note: The source distinguishes trailing T. majus from bush T. minus; no named cultivar is implied.

height.reason: The cited source describes varying trailing forms rather than a single reliable mature height for this type.

spread.reason: A cultivar-independent mature spread is not established for the represented type.

spacing.reason: Outdoor planting distances are not a universal indoor pod count.

evidence.note: Extension recommends full sun for flowering; partial shade is tolerated with reduced bloom. This is outdoor exposure, not an indoor grow-light tier.

name: Purple Kohlrabi
variety: Purple-skinned kohlrabi horticultural type; exact cultivar unspecified
summary: A color/type identity within kohlrabi, not a named cultivar. Wisconsin Extension notes purple cultivars have colored skin and white flesh; Kew treats the botanical name Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes as a synonym of B. oleracea.

identity.short: Kohlrabi color type within Brassica oleracea
identity.guidance: Kew accepts Brassica oleracea and synonymizes the botanical varietal name gongylodes with that species. Wisconsin Extension describes purple-skinned kohlrabi cultivars as having white interior flesh. This entry represents the useful purple-skinned crop type only; no cultivar such as Delicacy Purple is inferred.

cultivation.short: Cool-season crop; keep soil evenly moist
cultivation.guidance: Wisconsin Extension recommends full sun and moist, well-drained soil rich in organic matter, and describes kohlrabi as a cool-weather crop that tolerates more heat than many cole crops. This is open-ground guidance; exact hydroponic conditions are not established.

growth.short: The edible swollen stem develops above the soil
growth.guidance: Kohlrabi's edible rounded portion is a thickened stem above the soil line, not a root or true bulb. The source describes multiple maturity types; a single cultivar-specific size is not assigned to this color type.

harvest.short: Harvest timing depends on the selected cultivar
harvest.guidance: Wisconsin Extension lists different maturity estimates for individual named cultivars. Because this profile does not resolve a cultivar, those day counts are not copied here; consult the specific seed packet for its maturity estimate.

problems.short: Prevent stress that can interrupt stem development
problems.guidance: The selected crop guide supports cool-season, moist-soil culture but does not establish a type-specific disease-resistance claim. Monitor the swollen stem and foliage for stress; diagnose symptoms before treatment.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: The source covers soil-grown kohlrabi, not hydroponic systems.

evidence.note: Crop-level habit; purple skin does not establish a distinct growth habit.

height.reason: No type-specific mature height is established.

spread.reason: No type-specific mature spread is established.

spacing.reason: Field spacing is not converted into indoor pod spacing.

evidence.note: Full-sun recommendation for outdoor soil culture; not an indoor grow-light requirement.

name: Resina Calendula
variety: Named supplier-listed cultivar/product 'Resina'; no formal cultivar registration asserted
summary: Fedco lists Resina as an open-pollinated Calendula officinalis seed product selected for resinous flowers. A Montana State University field comparison reports cultivar-specific observations; its trial results are not guarantees for home gardens.

identity.short: Resina product identity within Calendula officinalis
identity.guidance: Kew accepts Calendula officinalis. Fedco lists Resina as an open-pollinated seed product; the listing supports the product/cultivar name but does not establish formal registration. The Montana field trial also names Resina as a tested cultivar.

cultivation.short: Cool-weather flowering; full sun and room to grow
cultivation.guidance: Fedco describes Calendula as thriving in cool weather, flowering over a long season, and recommends full sun without crowding. These are supplier crop-level instructions, not Resina-specific controlled trials. Its listed 70-day maturity is a seller estimate, not a guaranteed Garden schedule.

growth.short: Resinous yellow-to-orange flowers in the product description
growth.guidance: Fedco describes Resina's medium-sized single blooms as primarily bright yellow, with some orange flowers, and notes the flowers are resinous. The page's general Calendula height range is crop-level, so no Resina-specific mature-size value is assigned.

harvest.guidance: The Montana trial hand-harvested flowers repeatedly and observed Resina beginning to flower a few days before Erfurter Orangefarbige under the trial conditions. This timing comparison is specific to that Montana trial and is not a universal first-harvest date.

problems.short: Aster yellows affected plants in the field trial
problems.guidance: The Montana field report recorded aster-yellows symptoms in Resina plots in 1998 and 1999. This documents susceptibility in those trials, not an estimate of risk in every location. No disease resistance is claimed.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: The product and field-trial sources do not establish hydroponic flower production.

growthHabits.reason: Selected evidence does not establish a controlled growth-habit value for Resina.

height.reason: Fedco's height range is general Calendula crop information, not specifically measured for Resina.

spread.reason: No Resina-specific mature spread is established.

spacing.reason: No Resina-specific home-garden or indoor system spacing is selected.

evidence.note: Fedco's general crop guidance; not a Resina-specific controlled-light result.
